nodes.label: User
nodes.rationale: A person registered to use the chatbot, uniquely identified by a normalized email address. Avoid: Account, member.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: A User's authenticated use of the application on one device. A User may have multiple Sessions. Avoid: Login, token.

nodes.label: Chat
nodes.rationale: A named conversation owned by one User and containing an ordered history of Messages. Avoid: Thread, room.

nodes.label: Message
nodes.rationale: One contribution to a Chat, authored by either its User or the Assistant. Avoid: Prompt, response.

nodes.label: Assistant
nodes.rationale: The chatbot participant that generates replies to User Messages. Avoid: Bot, AI user.

nodes.label: Postgres Service
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 Alpine container with database chatbot, user chatbot, port 5432, init script at docker/postgres/init.sql.

nodes.label: Main Flow (idea → ship)
nodes.rationale: Primary workflow route: grill-with-docs → optional prototype/handoff branch → to-spec/to-tickets or implement → tdd + code-review.

nodes.label: Smart Zone
nodes.rationale: The ~120k token context window within which the model still reasons sharply; handoff when approaching limit before to-tickets.

nodes.label: Standards Axis
nodes.rationale: Does the code conform to documented coding standards plus Fowler Refactoring ch.3 smell baseline; repo standards override baseline.

nodes.label: Spec Axis
nodes.rationale: Does the code faithfully implement the originating issue, PRD, or spec; reported separately from Standards to prevent one axis masking the other.

nodes.label: Fowler Smell Baseline
nodes.rationale: Fixed set of Fowler code smells from Refactoring ch.3 applied as judgement-call heuristics when repo documents nothing; repo documented standards always win.

nodes.label: In-process Dependency
nodes.rationale: Pure computation, in-memory state, no I/O; always deepenable, test through new interface directly.

nodes.label: Local-substitutable Dependency
nodes.rationale: Dependencies with local test stand-ins (PGLite, in-memory filesystem); deepenable if stand-in exists.

nodes.label: Remote but Owned (Ports & Adapters)
nodes.rationale: Own services across network boundary; define port at seam, inject transport adapter for production and in-memory adapter for tests.

nodes.label: True External (Mock)
nodes.rationale: Third-party services not controlled; deepened module takes external dependency as injected port with mock adapter in tests.

nodes.label: Seam Discipline
nodes.rationale: One adapter means hypothetical seam; two adapters means real seam. Internal seams stay private to implementation.

nodes.label: Design It Twice (Ousterhout)
nodes.rationale: Parallel sub-agent pattern to explore radically different interfaces; first idea is unlikely to be the best.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.rationale: Anything with an interface and implementation; scale-agnostic (function, class, package, tier-spanning slice). Avoid: unit, component, service.

nodes.label: Interface
nodes.rationale: Everything a caller must know: type signature, invariants, ordering, error modes, config, performance. Avoid: API, signature.

nodes.label: Depth
nodes.rationale: Leverage at the interface: behaviour exercisable per unit of interface learned. Deep = large behaviour behind small interface.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Michael Feathers: place to alter behaviour without editing in that place; where module interface lives. Avoid: boundary.

nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: Concrete thing satisfying an interface at a seam; describes role not substance.

nodes.label: Leverage
nodes.rationale: What callers get from depth: more capability per unit of interface learned.

nodes.label: Locality
nodes.rationale: What maintainers get from depth: change, bugs, knowledge, verification concentrate in one place.

nodes.label: Deletion Test
nodes.rationale: If deleting the module vanishes complexity it was pass-through; if complexity reappears across callers it earned its keep.

nodes.label: Tight Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Core discipline: one command that goes red on this specific bug; refuse to hypothesise without it.

nodes.label: Correct Seam
nodes.rationale: Test seam must exercise real bug pattern at call site; absence of correct seam is an architectural finding.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record
nodes.rationale: Records hard-to-reverse, surprising, trade-off decisions in docs/adr/ with sequential numbering; value is recording that and why.

nodes.label: CONTEXT-MAP.md
nodes.rationale: Lists multiple contexts, where they live, and how they relate; used when repo has more than one bounded context.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language
nodes.rationale: Active discipline to challenge terms, resolve overload, and write glossary and ADRs as they crystallise; CONTEXT.md is glossary only.

nodes.label: 01 — Register a User and establish a Session
nodes.norm_label: 01 — register a user and establish a session

nodes.label: GET /auth/me
nodes.rationale: Browser uses access cookie to prove an active Session and retrieve the current public User.

nodes.label: Access JWT
nodes.rationale: Contains only User identifier, Session identifier, issued-at time, and expiry time.

nodes.label: Server-backed Session
nodes.rationale: Unknown, revoked, or absolutely expired Sessions are rejected even when JWT signature and expiry are valid so revoked Sessions stop working immediately.

nodes.label: Public User
nodes.rationale: Response exposes only User identifier, email, and creation time; internal password and Session fields never appear.

nodes.label: Session Guard
nodes.rationale: Reusable Session guard can protect later private chatbot endpoints.

nodes.label: Dual JWT and Session Validation
nodes.rationale: Authentication must validate both the JWT and its server-backed Session so revoked or expired Sessions stop working immediately.

nodes.label: Sign In
nodes.rationale: Registered User signs in with email and password, receives an independent device Session, and can access the current User endpoint.

nodes.label: Independent Device Session
nodes.rationale: Valid credentials create a new independent Session; E2E tests demonstrate separate Sessions for registration and subsequent sign-in.

nodes.label: Sign-in Abuse Controls
nodes.rationale: Temporary limits apply independently to normalized email and source IP without permanently locking a User; limits recover after their window.

nodes.label: Dummy Password Hash
nodes.rationale: Unknown-email verification uses a fixed dummy password hash to reduce timing differences.

nodes.label: Uniform Sign-in Failure Response
nodes.rationale: Failed attempts must not reveal whether an email exists; unknown email and incorrect password return the same status and response body.

nodes.label: Email Normalization
nodes.rationale: Sign-in normalizes email identically to registration.

nodes.label: Origin and Input Rejection
nodes.rationale: Missing or disallowed origins and invalid or unknown input fields are rejected.

nodes.label: POST /auth/register
nodes.rationale: HTTP contract that creates a User and Session and sets access_token and refresh_token cookies, returning a Public User. Ticket 01 implements this endpoint.
